questions.question: [NEET 2020 | Biology] Synapsis of homologous chromosomes occurs during:
questions.solution: ## Answer: **(B) Zygotene** --- ## Step-by-Step Explanation: ### The Five Substages of Prophase I (Meiosis I): | Stage | Key Event | |-------|-----------| | **Leptotene** | Chromosomes condense; homologs begin to approach each other | | **Zygotene** | **Synapsis occurs** - homologous chromosomes pair up completely | | **Pachytene** | Bivalents formed; crossing over takes place | | **Diplotene** | Homologs repel and start to separate; chiasmata visible | | **Diakinesis** | Further condensation; chromosomes move to poles | --- ## Understanding Synapsis: **Synapsis** = the process of precise pairing/alignment of homologous chromosomes - **During Zygotene**: Homologous chromosomes align perfectly along their entire length through a protein structure called the **synaptonemal complex** - This brings paternal and maternal chromosomes into close physical proximity - This is essential for crossing over (which occurs in pachytene) --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong: - **(A) Leptotene**: Only the BEGINNING of chromosome condensation; homologs START approaching but don't pair completely - **(C) Pachytene**: Synapsis is already COMPLETE here; this is when crossing over actively occurs - **(D) Diplotene**: Homologs are SEPARATING apart, not pairing --- ## Key Formula/Fact to Remember: **"ZYGotene = pairing (ZY-GY coupling)"** Think of Zygotene as the stage where chromosomes "**get together**" (zyga- means yoke/join in Greek)
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: [NEET 2021 | Biology] Crossing over (exchange of segments between non-sister chromatids) occurs during:
questions.solution: # Answer: **(C) Pachytene** ## Step-by-Step Explanation ### Stages of Prophase I (Meiosis I): | Stage | Events | |-------|--------| | **Leptotene** | Chromosomes condense into thin threads; centrioles move to poles | | **Zygotene** | Homologous chromosomes begin to pair (synapsis starts) | | **Pachytene** | **Bivalents fully formed; CROSSING OVER OCCURS** | | **Diplotene** | Homologous chromosomes start to separate; chiasmata visible | ## Why Pachytene? Crossing over requires: 1. \u₂₇₁₃ Homologous chromosomes completely paired (bivalents formed) 2. \u₂₇₁₃ Synaptonemal complex fully established 3. \u₂₇₁₃ Non-sister chromatids in close contact for exchange 4. \u₂₇₁₃ Enzymatic machinery ready for recombination **All these conditions are optimally met during pachytene.** ## Why Other Options Are Wrong: - **(A) Leptotene**: Chromosomes are unpaired; synapsis hasn't begun - **(B) Zygotene**: Pairing is just beginning (synapsis in progress); bivalents not complete - **(D) Diplotene**: Homologous chromosomes are **separating**; crossing over has already been completed ## Key Fact to Remember: **Pachytene = Peak Recombination Stage** - The longest stage of prophase I - Allows time for crossing over to be completed - Produces chiasmata (visible points of contact between exchanged segments)
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: [NEET 2017 | Biology] Correct sequence of Prophase I substages:
questions.solution: # Correct Answer: **(A) Leptotene-Zygotene-Pachytene-Diplotene-Diakinesis** --- ## Step-by-Step Explanation of Each Substage: | Substage | What Happens | Key Feature | |----------|--------------|------------| | **Leptotene** | Chromosomes condense as thin threads; homologous chromosomes begin pairing | Chromosomes appear "thin" | | **Zygotene** | Homologous chromosomes pair (synapsis) | Pairing occurs; bivalents form | | **Pachytene** | Bivalents are fully formed; chromosomes appear thick; **crossing over occurs** | Chromosomes appear "thick" | | **Diplotene** | Homologous chromosomes start to repel each other; remain attached at chiasmata | Separation begins | | **Diakinesis** | Chiasmata move toward chromosome ends (terminalization); chromosomes maximally condensed | Final separation stage | --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong: - **(B)** Pachytene before Zygotene is incorrect - synapsis (pairing) must occur before thick chromosome formation - **(C)** Zygotene before Leptotene is wrong - condensation occurs first in Leptotene - **(D)** Diplotene before Pachytene is incorrect - pairing must be complete before separation begins --- ## Key Memory Aid: **"LZPDD"** - Remember the **L**eptotene-**Z**ygotene-**P**achytene-**D**iplotene-**D**iakinesis sequence The progression follows the pairing and separation of homologous chromosomes logically and chronologically during meiosis I.
